Indigo System.name: Indigo
Indigo System.description: Indigo is the central gas giant of the system. Its atmosphere and rings contain deuterium-rich resources that support fuel extraction, refining, shipping, and military logistics. The system's inhabited and industrial sites are primarily moons, stations, depots, outposts, extraction platforms, and transfer lanes in orbit around Indigo. Route terms such as inward, outward, higher, and lower refer to position relative to Indigo's gravity well.

Indigo System.name: Orbit Bands
Indigo System.description: Indigo traffic is organized into broad orbital bands for route planning. The bands represent relative altitude around the gas giant rather than precise orbital mechanics. Band position affects travel time, fuel use, and route risk. Transfers within the same band are treated differently from moves that descend toward Indigo or climb away from it.

Indigo System.name: Low Orbit
Indigo System.description: Low orbit is the innermost operational band around Indigo. It is closest to the planet's gravity well and is mainly used by military, industrial, and specialized traffic. Descending into low orbit can be fuel-efficient, but departing from it with cargo requires significant fuel or tug support. Civilian freight normally uses this band only when a destination or contract requires it.

Indigo System.name: Ring Orbit
Indigo System.description: Ring orbit is the band associated with Indigo's rings and nearby industrial infrastructure. It contains extraction sites, refineries, depots, yards, and corporate facilities. Same-band travel in ring orbit is common, but distances around Indigo can still be large. Ring orbit is economically important because of deuterium extraction and related processing.

Indigo System.name: High Orbit
Indigo System.description: High orbit is a major operating band for civilian shipping, staging, and routine bluFreight work. It is farther from Indigo than the inner industrial bands while remaining connected to the main orbital network. Many stable stations, moons, and freight routes use this band. High orbit generally offers lower climb costs than inner bands but still requires route planning around Indigo.

Indigo System.name: Outer Orbit
Indigo System.description: Outer orbit is the distant operating band around Indigo. Travel times are longer, facilities are more dispersed, and outward transfers require additional fuel compared with many inner-system routes. Sites in this band are often remote, specialized, scientific, strategic, or locally self-reliant. Tug support may be useful for heavy cargo moving outward.

Indigo System.name: Transfer Lanes
Indigo System.description: Transfer lanes are named routing structures used for organized movement through the system. They function as staging paths, traffic corridors, or handoff points rather than settlements. Ships use them to manage transfers between moons, stations, orbit bands, and local destinations. Their value depends on current traffic, geometry, security, and cargo requirements.

Indigo System.name: Approach Variability
Indigo System.description: Approach variability measures how much local positioning uncertainty affects arrival at a destination. Low variability means the destination is close to its parent moon, station, or expected approach point. High variability means the final leg may involve wider local movement, shifting traffic, or a more restrictive docking window. BUDDE includes this factor when estimating routes.

Moons.name: Cat's Eye
Moons.description: Cat's Eye is a high-orbit moon used as the baseline for local bluFreight navigation. Anchor Station lies near Cat's Eye at the 0-degree reference position around Indigo. The nearby Ring Transfer Lane connects the moon to freight movement between high orbit and the ring-orbit band.

Moons.name: Corkscrew
Moons.description: Corkscrew is a high-orbit moon located in the same orbital band as Cat's Eye. Measured from Anchor Station at Cat's Eye, it lies 110 degrees prograde, or counterclockwise, around Indigo. UFP Outpost Delta operates at Corkscrew and supports Union security and routing activity in that sector.

Moons.name: Peltier
Moons.description: Peltier is a high-orbit moon in the main civilian traffic network. From Anchor Station at Cat's Eye, it lies 125 degrees retrograde, or clockwise, around Indigo within the same orbital band. Arcworks Fuel Depot and Baron's Market are located there, with local traffic centered on fuel supply and trade.

Moons.name: Oxblood
Moons.description: Oxblood is a ring-orbit moon positioned one orbital band inward from Cat's Eye, toward Indigo. From Anchor Station, it lies 35 degrees prograde, or counterclockwise, around the planet. The Refinery and Yard at Oxblood serve fuel processing, repair work, and industrial freight traffic.

Moons.name: Patch
Moons.description: Patch is a ring-orbit moon positioned one orbital band inward from Cat's Eye, toward Indigo. From Anchor Station, it lies 160 degrees prograde, or counterclockwise, around the planet. The Low Orbit Transfer Lane and UFP Outpost Bravo place Patch on both transfer routes and Union logistical lines.

Moons.name: Onion Skin
Moons.description: Onion Skin is a ring-orbit moon positioned one orbital band inward from Cat's Eye, toward Indigo. From Anchor Station, it lies 60 degrees retrograde, or clockwise, around the planet. Arcworks Operations Hub and Arcworks Militia Barracks are the main local facilities for corporate command and security.

Moons.name: Shooter
Moons.description: Shooter is a low-orbit moon positioned two orbital bands inward from Cat's Eye, deeper in Indigo's gravity well. From Anchor Station, it lies 80 degrees prograde, or counterclockwise, around the planet. Shooter contains UFP Indigo System Administration and UFP Outpost Alpha, the main Union administrative and security sites in that band.

Moons.name: Sulphide
Moons.description: Sulphide is a low-orbit moon positioned two orbital bands inward from Cat's Eye, deeper in Indigo's gravity well. From Anchor Station, it lies 110 degrees retrograde, or clockwise, around the planet. Indigo Station and the Deep Space Transfer Lane connect Sulphide to civic station traffic and long-range route planning.

Moons.name: Clambroth
Moons.description: Clambroth is an outer-orbit moon positioned one orbital band outward from Cat's Eye, farther from Indigo. From Anchor Station, it lies 145 degrees prograde, or counterclockwise, around the planet. The High Orbit Transfer Lane and Condenser Columns support transfer staging and fuel-related extraction work in this remote band.

Moons.name: End-of-Day
Moons.description: End-of-Day is an outer-orbit moon positioned one orbital band outward from Cat's Eye, farther from Indigo. From Anchor Station, it lies 35 degrees retrograde, or clockwise, around the planet. UFP Science Station is located there and serves as a remote Union research site.

Transfer Lanes.name: Ring Transfer Lane
Transfer Lanes.description: Ring Transfer Lane is a named traffic corridor associated with Cat's Eye and routes into the ring-orbit band. It provides staging, alignment, and handoff points for ships moving between high orbit and ring-adjacent destinations. Its local approach profile is wider than a station approach because ships use the lane as a routing structure rather than a fixed berth.

Transfer Lanes.name: Low Orbit Transfer Lane
Transfer Lanes.description: Low Orbit Transfer Lane is a structured traffic corridor near Patch in ring orbit. It supports traffic descending toward low orbit or climbing out toward higher bands. The lane is used for staging, fuel planning, and route coordination where Indigo's gravity well has a major effect on cargo movement.

Transfer Lanes.name: High Orbit Transfer Lane
Transfer Lanes.description: High Orbit Transfer Lane is a named transfer corridor near Clambroth in outer orbit. It supports long-range staging between the outer band and the main high-orbit traffic network. Ships use the lane to align for extended routes, exchange cargo assignments, and reduce inefficient repositioning in the outer system.

Transfer Lanes.name: Deep Space Transfer Lane
Transfer Lanes.description: Deep Space Transfer Lane is a long-range staging corridor near Sulphide in low orbit. It supports route planning for traffic leaving the inner system or entering from distant lanes. The lane handles fuel-sensitive transfers where low-orbit positioning, departure timing, and long-haul alignment are operationally important.

Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.name: Anchor Station
Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.description: Anchor Station is a civilian station near Cat's Eye in high orbit. It serves as the primary local reference point for bluFreight operations and routine traffic planning. Its position at the 0-degree reference mark around Indigo makes it a common starting point for routes, contracts, and comparisons to other moons and facilities.

Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.name: Refinery
Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.description: The Refinery is an industrial facility at Oxblood in ring orbit. It processes deuterium-rich materials from Indigo's rings and supports fuel production for civilian, corporate, and military traffic. Freight moving through the Refinery commonly includes processed fuel, industrial supplies, spare parts, and maintenance cargo.

Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.name: Yard
Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.description: The Yard is an industrial facility at Oxblood in ring orbit. It handles ship repair, hull work, salvage processing, and heavy equipment staging. Its proximity to the Refinery places repair capacity close to fuel processing and other industrial freight activity.

Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.name: Indigo Station
Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.description: Indigo Station is a major station near Sulphide in low orbit. It supports municipal, civilian, and operational traffic within the inner system. Its location deep in Indigo's gravity well connects ordinary station life with demanding low-orbit logistics, including fuel planning, tug support, and traffic coordination.

Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.name: UFP Science Station
Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.description: UFP Science Station is a Union research facility at End-of-Day in outer orbit. It supports scientific observation, technical studies, and specialized storage or processing work far from the denser inner traffic bands. Its remote position requires regular freight service for equipment, fuel, personnel supplies, and station maintenance.

Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.name: Arcworks Operations Hub
Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.description: Arcworks Operations Hub is a corporate command and station facility on Onion Skin in ring orbit. It coordinates Arcworks extraction schedules, industrial traffic, security assignments, and local administration. The hub anchors Arcworks activity around Onion Skin and links corporate planning directly to nearby ring-orbit infrastructure.

Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.name: Arcworks Militia Barracks
Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.description: Arcworks Militia Barracks is an armed corporate security facility on Onion Skin. It houses militia personnel, equipment, and supplies used to protect Arcworks infrastructure and enforce local control. The barracks supports escort activity, route security, and rapid response near Arcworks operations in ring orbit.

Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.name: UFP Indigo System Administration
Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.description: UFP Indigo System Administration is a Union administrative complex on Shooter in low orbit. It coordinates regulatory authority, contract oversight, traffic priorities, and official system policy. Its placement near UFP Outpost Alpha keeps civil administration close to Union security infrastructure and high-priority logistics routes.

Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.name: UFP Outpost Alpha
Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.description: UFP Outpost Alpha is a Union military outpost on Shooter in low orbit. It supports patrol operations, security response, and official freight handling near UFP Indigo System Administration. Supplies, munitions, rations, and administrative cargo pass through the outpost as part of Union activity in the inner system.

Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.name: UFP Outpost Bravo
Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.description: UFP Outpost Bravo is a Union military outpost on Patch in ring orbit. It supports Union patrols and logistics in the ring-adjacent traffic band, close to the Low Orbit Transfer Lane. The outpost handles military supplies, escort coordination, and security operations around nearby industrial and transfer routes.

Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.name: UFP Outpost Delta
Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.description: UFP Outpost Delta is a Union military outpost at Corkscrew in high orbit. It monitors traffic along the high-orbit arc from Cat's Eye, supports escorted routing, and receives Union logistics cargo. Its position in the same orbit band as Anchor Station places it on a major civilian and military transit path.

Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.name: Arcworks Fuel Depot
Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.description: Arcworks Fuel Depot is a fuel storage and distribution facility on Peltier in high orbit. It handles deuterium supplies and related equipment for Arcworks traffic, commercial buyers, and onward shipment. The depot provides Arcworks with a practical foothold in high-orbit fuel logistics outside the inner industrial bands.

Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.name: Baron's Market
Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.description: Baron's Market is a commercial station on Peltier in high orbit. It serves as a market, brokerage point, and civilian trade hub for cargo moving through the local high-orbit network. Traffic at the station includes consumer goods, industrial parts, fuel contracts, and opportunistic freight from multiple factions and private operators.

Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.name: Condenser Columns
Stations, Outposts, and Facilities.description: Condenser Columns is an industrial extraction and processing site near Clambroth in outer orbit. It collects and prepares fuel-related materials for storage, refinement, or shipment elsewhere in the system. Its remote location links outer-orbit resource work to the broader deuterium supply chain.

Factions and Institutions.name: bluFreight
Factions and Institutions.description: bluFreight is a civilian logistics company operating in the Indigo system. It moves cargo for government, municipal, corporate, and local clients, with most of its protected work tied to Union of Free Planets contracts. The company is not a military organization, but its Union alignment affects access, escort coverage, and how other factions treat its ships.

Factions and Institutions.name: Union of Free Planets
Factions and Institutions.description: The Union of Free Planets is the interplanetary state that asserted control over Indigo after the system's deuterium value was confirmed. It presents its role as security, lawful trade, and market stabilization while also securing fuel, infrastructure, and strategic depth. In Indigo the Union acts as regulator, patrol authority, military power, and major contract client for logistics firms such as bluFreight.

Factions and Institutions.name: Arcworks
Factions and Institutions.description: Arcworks is a mining and industrial corporation with operations in Indigo that predate formal Union control. It operates extraction sites, fuel infrastructure, command facilities, and armed security forces. Arcworks treats Union-backed authority as an external claim over infrastructure that the company considers locally built and commercially earned.

Factions and Institutions.name: Blister
Factions and Institutions.description: Blister is a loose armed faction operating through raids, tribute, negotiated passage, and local control of vulnerable routes. Union authorities classify it as predatory and unlawful, but Blister captains also maintain practical arrangements where force, reputation, and payment define safe movement. Its presence raises the political and security cost of freight traffic.

Factions and Institutions.name: Station Municipal Authorities
Factions and Institutions.description: Station Municipal Authorities are local civic administrations responsible for keeping inhabited stations supplied and functional. They manage utilities, food supply, medical needs, berthing priorities, and public services. Their contracts usually concern continuity of life and station maintenance rather than military objectives or corporate expansion.

Clients.name: Station Municipal
Clients.description: Station Municipal clients are civic authorities purchasing freight service for inhabited stations and public facilities. Their contracts cover practical needs such as agricultural shipments, medical supplies, deuterium for utilities, replacement parts, and other cargo required for station stability.

ships_and_classes.name: Hauler
ships_and_classes.description: Hauler-class ships are standard civilian freight vessels built for bulk cargo movement. They carry larger loads than couriers or shuttles but accelerate slowly and perform poorly on steep climbs out of lower orbit bands. Haulers are the baseline craft for routine bluFreight contracts.

ships_and_classes.name: Courier
ships_and_classes.description: Courier-class ships are light freight vessels designed for small, time-sensitive cargo. They trade capacity for speed, route flexibility, and lower handling overhead. Couriers are suited to medical cargo, documents, priority components, and other shipments where arrival time matters more than tonnage.

ships_and_classes.name: Tug
ships_and_classes.description: Tug-class vessels are utility craft built to move mass through difficult orbital maneuvers. They carry little cargo directly but assist heavier ships with climbs, repositioning, and other high-burn route segments. Tugs are especially valuable when loaded freighters need to move outward from deeper orbit bands.

ships_and_classes.name: Shuttle
ships_and_classes.description: Shuttle-class craft are short-range vessels used for local transfers, station errands, personnel movement, and small cargo hops. They are not designed for heavy freight or long independent routes. Their value comes from access, responsiveness, and the ability to handle nearby destinations without committing a larger freighter.

ships_and_classes.name: Probe
ships_and_classes.description: Probe-class platforms are stationary or near-stationary sensor assets. They monitor traffic, detect contacts, and provide local awareness for routes or facilities. Probes do not haul cargo and have limited survivability if directly attacked.

ships_and_classes.name: Kestrel
ships_and_classes.description: The Kestrel is a Union interceptor built for rapid response and pursuit. It emphasizes speed, maneuverability, and enough armament to challenge raiders or escort hostile contacts away from civilian traffic. Kestrels are commonly associated with patrol coverage and convoy security.

ships_and_classes.name: Pelican
ships_and_classes.description: The Pelican is a Union logistics freighter used for protected cargo movement. It carries more military support and defensive capability than a civilian hauler while retaining substantial freight capacity. Pelicans are used for official supply runs, outpost support, and higher-risk Union logistics work.

ships_and_classes.name: Dragoon
ships_and_classes.description: The Dragoon is a Blister interceptor used for intimidation, pursuit, and armed control of routes. It is not the fastest interceptor in Indigo, but it is durable enough for raids and close engagements. Dragoons support Blister's practice of turning route insecurity into leverage.

ships_and_classes.name: MK-IV
ships_and_classes.description: The MK-IV is an Arcworks interceptor adapted from industrial hull designs. It combines workship durability with weapons and armor for local defense. MK-IVs reflect Arcworks' reliance on practical industrial hardware converted for militia and infrastructure security roles.

ships_and_classes.name: MM-IX
ships_and_classes.description: The MM-IX is an Arcworks utility platform retrofitted for armed service. It retains the mass, mounting points, and rugged systems of a work platform while carrying equipment suitable for defense and enforcement. The class is used around corporate facilities where industrial support and security overlap.

cargo_types.name: Deuterium
cargo_types.description: Deuterium is Indigo's primary strategic resource. It is used as fusion fuel, industrial feedstock, and station energy reserve. Control of deuterium extraction, processing, storage, and shipment drives much of the system's military, corporate, and political conflict.

cargo_types.name: Munitions
cargo_types.description: Munitions are military cargo used to supply outposts, patrol forces, and armed facilities. They include ammunition, missile components, weapons packages, and related handling equipment. Munitions shipments are sensitive because they directly affect faction combat readiness and route security.

cargo_types.name: Medical
cargo_types.description: Medical cargo includes medicines, surgical supplies, diagnostic equipment, replacement stock, and emergency treatment materials. It is typically compact but time-sensitive. Stations, outposts, research sites, and ships all depend on medical shipments to keep personnel alive and operational.

cargo_types.name: Rations
cargo_types.description: Rations are preserved food and basic consumables for crews, stations, and outposts. They are logistically simple but operationally essential. Interruptions in ration supply can quickly turn routine isolation into a station emergency.

cargo_types.name: Consumer Goods
cargo_types.description: Consumer goods are civilian trade cargo for station residents, markets, and local businesses. They include household items, personal electronics, replacement goods, luxuries, and other non-military supplies. Their movement indicates ordinary commercial life continuing inside the war-zone economy.

cargo_types.name: Agricultural
cargo_types.description: Agricultural cargo includes food crops, seed stock, hydroponic materials, nutrient media, and equipment for station food systems. Municipal authorities rely on these shipments to maintain local food production and reduce dependence on imported rations.

cargo_types.name: VIP
cargo_types.description: VIP cargo refers to protected passenger movement for officials, specialists, negotiators, executives, or other high-priority persons. These contracts are small by mass but high in security and timing requirements. A VIP shipment may affect route approvals, escort decisions, and faction attention.

characters.name: BASIL
characters.description: BASIL is the BluFreight Automated Scheduling, Interchange, and Liaison system assigned to Indigo operations. It handles dispatch messaging, contract framing, operational reminders, and status updates for bluFreight traffic. BASIL represents the company's scheduling and administrative layer in the system.

characters.name: BUDDE
characters.description: BUDDE, the Benchmark Unified Directions Dedicated Engine, is the navigation optimizer used for route efficiency, burn planning, and transfer comparison. It evaluates distance, orbit-band changes, direction of travel, and approach variability. BUDDE's recommendations focus on movement efficiency rather than political or commercial judgment.

characters.name: Capt. Soren Nnadi
characters.description: Captain Soren Nnadi is a bluFreight hauler captain. He handles standard civilian freight work and is associated with steady route execution, crew management, and practical contract movement. His role represents the ordinary line-captain side of bluFreight operations.

characters.name: Capt. Tamsin Rook
characters.description: Captain Tamsin Rook is a bluFreight shuttle captain. She specializes in short-range transfers, local-access routes, station errands, and small cargo movement. Her work covers destinations where a full freighter is unnecessary or inefficient.

characters.name: Capt. Laleh Mercer
characters.description: Captain Laleh Mercer is a bluFreight courier captain. She handles light freight, priority cargo, and routes where speed is more important than carrying capacity. Her assignments commonly involve time-sensitive shipments and smaller loads.

characters.name: Capt. Jonas Vale
characters.description: Captain Jonas Vale is a bluFreight heavy freight captain. He handles large, slow cargo movements where mass, fuel cost, and route planning dominate the operation. His work is closely tied to the practical limits of moving heavy freight through Indigo's orbit bands.

characters.name: Capt. Mara Ibarra
characters.description: Captain Mara Ibarra is a bluFreight tug captain. She handles assist maneuvers, heavy climbs, and mass-control work for ships that need support moving through Indigo's gravity well. Her role is centered on propulsion assistance rather than direct cargo capacity.

characters.name: Cmdr. Elias Thorne
characters.description: Commander Elias Thorne is a Union officer associated with patrol authority and traffic discipline in Indigo. He represents the UFP security presence around civilian shipping, outposts, and escorted routes. His authority is tied to Union enforcement of order and route control.

characters.name: Capt. Hadrik Venn
characters.description: Captain Hadrik Venn is a Blister captain active in Indigo route politics and armed freight encounters. He represents Blister's use of negotiation, tribute, threat, and force as tools of movement control. His presence marks routes where security depends on more than distance and fuel.

characters.name: Port Marshal Celia Wren
characters.description: Port Marshal Celia Wren is a station authority responsible for berth discipline, traffic queues, manifests, and local port operations. Her work sits between civilian station life and freight movement. She represents the administrative control needed to keep station traffic orderly.
